audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 2.17%, Shanghai in rialzo dell'1.28%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.3%, il VIX è sceso del 3.91%. Il DXY è in calo dello 0.15%, a 99.89 L'oro è in rialzo dello 0.5%, a $4357.7 l'oncia. Il petrolio è in calo del 1.97%, a $92.39 Il rendimento del US 10Y è in rialzo dello 0.35%, al 4.55%. Il BTP 10Y è stabile, al 3.73%.

La situazione in Ucraina continua a rappresentare una sfida fiscale e finanziaria per il paese. Inoltre, la Cina sta cercando di rafforzare la sua influenza in Asia, in particolare con la Corea del Nord.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi. La BCE ha annunciato i principali traguardi per l'attuazione del quadro di rendicontazione integrata.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i sessantamila dollari, con una lieve flessione del 0,28%. Gli ETF su Bitcoin hanno registrato un deflusso netto di circa 326 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle preoccupazioni legate all'inflazione. 
  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna lo 0,90%, raggiungendo i mille e seicentosettantacinque dollari. Solana e BNB mostrano una crescita più significativa, rispettivamente dell'1,61% e dell'1,44%, arrivando a 66,63 e 602,24 dollari. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 10, in zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 2.17%, Shanghai up 1.28%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed up 0.3%, the VIX fell 3.91%. The DXY is down 0.15%, at 99.89 Gold is up 0.5%, at $4357.7 per ounce. Oil is down 1.97%, at $92.39 The US 10Y yield is up 0.35%, to 4.55%. The BTP 10Y is stable, at 3.73%. The situation in Ukraine continues to represent a fiscal and financial challenge for the country. Furthermore, China is seeking to strengthen its influence in Asia, particularly with North Korea. No major macroeconomic data out today. The ECB has announced the main targets for the implementation of the integrated reporting framework. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above sixty thousand dollars, with a slight decline of 0.28%. Bitcoin ETFs have recorded a net outflow of around $326 million. This movement could be influenced by concerns related to inflation. Among altcoins, Ethereum gains 0.9%, reaching $1,675 Solana and BNB show more significant growth, respectively 1.61% and 1.44%, reaching $66.63 and $602.24 The Fear & Greed Index is at 10, in Extreme Fear zone, suggests caution on investors. No macro data on the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The FCAS fighter jet looks like it’s dead. Could that be a good thing?
articles.snippet: The FCAS fighter jet looks like it’s dead. Could that be a good thing? Expert comment jon.wallace 8 June 2026 FCAS was already competing with the GCAP project and Swedish and Turkish fighters. Europe should combine its efforts. European states have known since the early 2000s that they will need to develop a replacement for their existing fighter aircraft. Concepts for a ‘next generation fighter programme’ go beyond the development of just a jet. Plans to include a combat ‘cloud’ and uncrewed systems to operate alongside fighter jets have been around for almost the same amount of time. articles.title: From Pyongyang to Primorsk: When Sanctions Evasion Becomes System Design
articles.snippet: Rarely a week passes without a new story about Russia’s shadow fleet. Tankers catch fire in the Mediterranean, are added to sanctions lists, or are boarded while passing through European waters. But the bigger story is not the vessels that are caught, but those that aren’t — ships moving between registries, ports, shell companies, and service providers that obscure their ties to Russia while keeping a sanctioned state afloat. articles.title: The digitalisation of banking and social media: implications for deposit pricing
articles.snippet: by Michael Brei, Giulio Cornelli, Leonardo Gambacorta, Boris Hofmann This paper examines the implications of two coincident digital trends – the digitalisation of banking and the widespread adoption of social media – for the pricing of deposits in the United States. Using branch-level data, we analyse how both trends interact to influence the level of deposit rates as well as their adjustment to changes in the policy rate.

articles.title: Is Skepticism Ukraine’s Foreign Policy Playbook?
articles.snippet: Welcome to The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest of Ukrainian commentary and analysis from across the political spectrum only for War on the Rocks members. articles.title: Airfares Are Set to Rise Again as the Fuel Crisis Deepens
articles.snippet: Prices for flights will shoot up again if fuel costs stay high, the chief of British Airways has warned.
